In the mathematical theory of [[Probability theory|probability]] and [[Measure theory|measure]], a '''sub-probability''' measure is a [[Measure (mathematics)|measure]] that is closely related to [[probability measure]]s. While probability measures always assign the value&nbsp;1 to the underlying set, sub-probability measures assign a value lesser than or equal to&nbsp;1 to the underlying set.

== Definition ==

Let <math> \mu </math> be a [[Measure (mathematics)|measure]] on the [[measurable space]]  <math> (X, \mathcal A) </math>.

Then <math> \mu </math> is called a sub-probability measure if <math> \mu(X) \leq 1 </math>.<ref name="Klenke247" /><ref name="Kallenberg30" />

== Properties ==

In measure theory, the following implications hold between measures:
<math display=block>\text{probability} \implies \text{sub-probability} \implies \text{finite} \implies \sigma\text{-finite}</math>

So every probability measure is a sub-probability measure, but the converse is not true. Also every sub-probability measure is a [[finite measure]] and a [[σ-finite measure]], but the converse is again not true.
